newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel mediators' mandate not extended.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel mediators' mandate not extended.

text.p: The mandate of two court appointed mediators in negotiations between Eurotunnel SA/Plc and its creditor banks will not be extended when it expires on Monday, sources close to the talks said.
Earlier, Eurotunnel shares were suspended in Paris, London and Brussels with the company saying it wished to avoid sepeculation causing a false market.
The company owes the banks over 8.0 billion stg in junior debt and suspended interest payments on the loans last September.
Protracted negotiations since then have so far failed to reach agreement on restructuring the debt.
The Paris court appointed the mediators, Robert Badinter and Lord Wakeham earlier this year in an attempt to bring the two sides closer together.
Sources said the Paris commercial court will meet this morning to consider the case but they said the position may not be clarified until Tuesday.
Both sides expect the court to allow negotiations to continue even though the usefullness of the mediators has been exhausted.

While a basic framework for restructuring the debt seems to have been in place for some time, the two sides still seem far apart on the price at which debt in the company can be swapped for shares and/or a convertible instrument.
Sources said court president Jean-Pierre Mattei has been considering the latest report by the mediators for some days and will make a ruling after taking into account what they say.
The freeze on interest payments is due to remain in place until March 14, 1997 unless an agreement is reached or creditors representing 66 percent of the debt decide to call the debt in.
One aspect which complicates the talks is that the loans in question fall under both English and French law which could create, if the talks break down, to a horrendous cross-border legal quagmire.
